sentences.text: This predator grew to a length of roughly seven meters and likely weighed around 1.2 tons.
Its head was broad and flat on the upper surface, topped by a noticeable ridge.
Friedrich von Huene first named the animal in 1932, with a full description following in 1933 alongside Charles Alfred Matley.
The initial study relied on three incomplete skulls discovered near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, India, inside the Lameta Formation.
Unfortunately, the specific specimen chosen as the standard reference has been lost since that time.
It is now securely placed within the Abelisauridae family, though von Huene originally grouped it with Allosauridae.
In 1964, Alick Walker proposed that the creature belonged to the Tyrannosauridae instead.
By 1986, José Bonaparte argued it was an abelisaurid, a view supported by later studies.
A 2004 analysis defined the group by the forward position of the frontonasal suture relative to the lacrimal bone.
The name itself merges the Greek word for the Indus River with the name of the Egyptian crocodile deity Sobek.
This animal roamed India during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian age, between approximately 70 and 66 million years ago.
